drivingQuestion: Is one flogged for slaughtering the second animal when that slaughter also carried a graver penalty for which he was not forewarned, and are the red heifer and the broken-necked heifer genuinely unfit slaughter?
outcomeNote: The heifer clause is finally attributed to R' Yoḥanan through R' Ḥiyya bar Abba, which removes both the contradiction from R' Yannai and Rav Ashi's difficulty with Reish Lakish.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְשֵׁנִי לְשֻׁלְחָנוֹ, אֲבָל רִאשׁוֹן לְשֻׁלְחָנוֹ וְשֵׁנִי לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה – פָּטוּר, דְּקָם לֵיהּ בִּדְרַבָּה מִינֵּיהּ.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:» The Rabbis in the mishna «taught» that one is liable when one of the animals is slaughtered for the sake of idol worship «only when he slaughtered» the «first» animal «for» the sake of «idol worship and» the «second» animal «for his» own «table. But» if he slaughtered the «first» animal «for his» own «table and» the «second» animal «for» the sake of «idol worship,» he is «exempt» from lashes for the second act of slaughter, «as he receives» only «the greater» punishment, that for idol worship, which is death.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן יוֹדְעִין אוֹתָהּ! אֶלָּא, פְּעָמִים שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ שָׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן לְשֻׁלְחָנוֹ וְשֵׁנִי לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה – חַיָּיב.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him: Even schoolchildren know this» halakha, that one who is liable to receive two punishments receives only the greater punishment. «Rather, sometimes, even if he slaughtered» the «first for his» own «table and» the «second for» the sake of «idol worship,» he is «liable» to receive lashes for the second act of slaughter.

segments.he: כְּגוֹן דְּאַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ מִשּׁוּם ״אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ״, וְלֹא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ מִשּׁוּם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּכִי אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ – פָּטוּר, כִּי לָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ נָמֵי – פָּטוּר.
segments.en: This occurs, «for example, where» the witnesses «forewarned him» before the second act of slaughter «with regard to» the prohibition of: «Itself and its offspring, but» they «did not forewarn him with regard to idol worship.» Since he is not punished for performing idol worship, he receives lashes for the less severe transgression. «And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: Since, had they forewarned him» with regard to idol worship he would have been «exempt» from lashes; therefore, even «if they did not forewarn him» with regard to idol worship, «he is also exempt» from lashes.

segments.he: וְאָזְדוּ לְטַעְמַיְיהוּ, דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר: חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת שׁוֹגְגִין, וְחַיָּיבֵי מַלְקוֹת שׁוֹגְגִין, וְדָבָר אַחֵר – רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אוֹמֵר: חַיָּיב, וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר: פָּטוּר.
segments.en: The Gemara notes: «And they» each «follow their» known lines of «reasoning» in this matter. «As when Rav Dimi came» to Babylonia from Eretz Yisrael «he said:» With regard to «those» who «unwittingly» performed a transgression for which one is «liable to» receive the «death» penalty if one performed it intentionally, «or those» who «unwittingly» performed a transgression for which one is «liable» to receive «lashes, and» that transgression also involved «another matter,» monetary payment, and they were forewarned with regard to the monetary penalty but not with regard to the lashes or the death penalty, «Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» He is «liable» to pay; «and Reish Lakish says:» He is «exempt.»

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אוֹמֵר: חַיָּיב, דְּהָא לָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ; וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר: פָּטוּר, דְּכֵיוָן דְּכִי אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ פָּטוּר – כִּי לָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ נָמֵי פָּטוּר.
segments.en: The Gemara clarifies the rationales for their statements. «Rabbi Yoḥanan says» that he is «liable; since they did not forewarn him» with regard to the severe transgression, he sinned unwittingly, and he remains liable only to pay the monetary payment. «And Reish Lakish says» that he is «exempt; since had they forewarned him» with regard to the severe transgression, he would have been «exempt» from the monetary payment, «when they did not forewarn him,» he is «also exempt.»

segments.he: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן בְּהָא – בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, אֲבָל בְּהָא – אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
segments.en: The Gemara notes: «And it is necessary» to state their disagreement with regard to both of these cases. «As, if it were taught to us» only «about this» case where one slaughters the mother for his private use and afterward slaughters its offspring for idol worship, perhaps only «in this» case involving the death penalty and lashes «does Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish say» that even if they did not forewarn the transgressor with regard to idol worship, he is still exempt from lashes for the prohibition of: Itself and its offspring, because the death penalty and lashes are similar in that they are both corporal punishments, and so the obligation of lashes does not take effect at all when the death penalty is potentially applicable. «But in that» case, involving the death penalty or lashes together with a monetary payment, «say that he agrees with Rabbi Yoḥanan» that the transgressor is liable to pay the monetary payment.

segments.he: וְאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָא, בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אֲבָל בְּהָא אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, צְרִיכָא.
segments.en: «And if» the disagreement «was stated» only «with regard to that» case, where one unwittingly performed a transgression involving the death penalty or lashes together with a transgression bearing a monetary payment, perhaps only «in that» case «does Rabbi Yoḥanan say» that he is liable to pay the monetary payment. «But in this» case, where one slaughtered an animal and its offspring, and the second animal was slaughtered for the sake of idol worship, which involves the death penalty and lashes, but without a forewarning with regard to the death penalty, «say that he agrees with Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish» that one is exempt from lashes. Therefore, it is «necessary» to state their disagreement with regard to both cases.

segments.he: וּפָרַת חַטָּאת שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה הִיא? וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: פָּרָה מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין, הוֹאִיל וְהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that Rabbi Shimon deems one who slaughters the red heifer of purification exempt from punishment for the prohibition of: Itself and its offspring, as that act of slaughter does not render the animal fit for consumption. The Gemara asks: «And» is the slaughter of «the» red «heifer of purification» considered an act of «slaughter that is unfit» for consumption? «But isn’t it taught» in a baraita: «Rabbi Shimon says:» A red «heifer,» even if it has been slaughtered and it is therefore prohibited to derive benefit from it, «is susceptible to the ritual impurity of food, since it had a time in which it was fit» for consumption?

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, פָּרָה נִפְדֵּית עַל גַּבֵּי מַעֲרַכְתָּהּ. אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: פָּרַת חַטָּאת אֵינָהּ מִשְׁנָה.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says» in explanation of Rabbi Shimon’s statement: «Rabbi Shimon would say» that the red «heifer can be redeemed» with money even once it has been slaughtered and placed «upon its pyre» in preparation for being burned. Therefore, Rabbi Shimon states that there could be a time when the heifer was fit for consumption, i.e., if it was redeemed. Why, then, does he deem one who slaughters it exempt from liability for transgressing the prohibition of: Itself and its offspring? «Rav Shemen bar Abba said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» The statement with regard to «the» red «heifer of purification is not» considered part of the «mishna,» and Rabbi Shimon agrees that its slaughterer is liable for transgressing the prohibition of: Itself and its offspring.

segments.he: וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה, לָאו שְׁחִיטָה רְאוּיָה הִיא? וְהָתְנַן: נִמְצָא הַהוֹרֵג עַד שֶׁלֹּא תֵּעָרֵף הָעֲגָלָה – תֵּצֵא וְתִרְעֶה בָּעֵדֶר. אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי: עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה אֵינָהּ מִשְׁנָה.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And is» the slaughter of the «heifer whose neck» was «to» have been «broken not» considered an act of «slaughter» that is «fit? But didn’t we learn» in a mishna (Sota 47a): If a heifer was set aside to have its neck broken to atone for the murder of an individual whose murderer was not known, and then «the murderer was found before the heifer’s neck was broken,» the heifer «shall go out and graze among the flock,» as it is not consecrated. Evidently, before its neck is broken, deriving benefit from it is not prohibited, and its slaughter would be one that is fit. «Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:» The statement with regard to «the heifer whose neck» was «to» have been «broken is not» considered part of the «mishna,» and Rabbi Shimon agrees that its slaughterer is liable for violating the prohibition of: Itself and its offspring.

segments.he: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: גְּבוּל שָׁמַעְתִּי בָּהּ, וְשָׁכַחְתִּי, וְנָסְבִין חַבְרַיָּא לוֹמַר: יְרִידָתָהּ לְנַחַל אֵיתָן אוֹסַרְתָּהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And does Rabbi Yannai» actually «say so? But doesn’t Rabbi Yannai say: I heard» the «boundary,» i.e., stage, beyond which the heifer is forbidden, «but I have forgotten» what it is; «but the group» of scholars «were inclined to say» that the heifer’s «descent to a hard valley,» where its neck is broken, «is» the action that «renders it forbidden?»

segments.he: וְאִם אִיתָא, לִישַׁנֵּי: כָּאן קוֹדֶם יְרִידָה, כָּאן לְאַחַר יְרִידָה.
segments.en: «And if it is so, let him resolve» the contradiction by saying: «Here,» where deriving benefit from the heifer is permitted, and its slaughterer is liable for transgressing the prohibition of: Itself and its offspring, it is referring to an act of slaughtering that is fit and is performed «before» the heifer’s «descent,» while «there,» in the mishna, where Rabbi Shimon holds that there is no liability for transgressing: Itself and its offspring, it is referring to slaughtering performed «after» its «descent.» At that time, deriving benefit from the heifer is already prohibited, and the slaughter is therefore not considered fit.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב פִּנְחָס בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי: אֲנַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ, עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה אֵינָהּ מִשְׁנָה. אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב פַּפֵּי קַשְׁיָא לַן, מִי אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ הָכִי?
segments.en: «Rav Pineḥas, son of Rav Ami, said: We taught» the statement «in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish» himself, not as a quote from Rabbi Yannai: The statement with regard to «the heifer whose neck is broken is not» considered part of the «mishna. Rav Ashi said: When we were» studying in «the study hall of Rav Pappi,» that statement was «difficult for us: Did Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish» actually «say» that it is not considered part of the mishna?

segments.he: וְהָא אִיתְּמַר, צִפּוֹרֵי מְצוֹרָע מֵאֵימָתַי נֶאֱסָרִין? רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מִשְּׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מִשְּׁעַת לְקִיחָה, וְאָמְרִינַן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ?
segments.en: «But it was stated» that amora’im engaged in a dispute concerning the following issue: «From when» is one «prohibited» from deriving benefit from «the leper’s birds? Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» One is prohibited «from the moment of» their «slaughter; and Reish Lakish says:» One is prohibited «from the moment» they are «taken» and designated to be a leper’s birds. «And we say: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish?»

His reasoning is that he «derives» it via verbal analogy «from» the terms: «“Taking [kiḥa]”» (Leviticus 14:4), with regard to the birds, and: «“Taking [kiḥa]”» (Deuteronomy 21:3), with regard to the «heifer whose neck is broken.» Consequently, just as deriving benefit from the heifer whose neck is broken is prohibited from the time of its selection, so too must deriving benefit from these birds be prohibited from the time of their selection. Clearly, then, Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish holds that deriving benefit from the heifer whose neck is broken is prohibited while it is still alive. Therefore, its slaughter is one that does not render the animal fit for consumption. Accordingly, Rabbi Shimon would exempt its slaughterer from the prohibition of: Itself and its offspring, as is taught in the mishna.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה אֵינָהּ מִשְׁנָה.
segments.en: «Rather, Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» The statement with regard to the «heifer whose neck is broken is not» considered part of «the mishna,» and this resolution of the difficulty was articulated by Rabbi Yoḥanan rather than Reish Lakish.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש: לא שנו אלא
moves.summary: Reish Lakish limits the Rabbis' liability to where the first animal was slaughtered for idolatry
moves.about: the mishna's liability for slaughtering the second animal applies only where the first was slaughtered for idolatry and the second for his table

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבי יוחנן: זו, אפילו תינוקות של בית רבן יודעין אותה!
moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan dismisses the limitation as stating only what schoolchildren know
moves.about: that Reish Lakish's limitation states only the obvious rule that a greater penalty absorbs a lesser one, so it cannot be the mishna's point

moves.cueHe: אלא, פעמים שאפילו שחט ראשון לשלחנו ושני לעבודה זרה – חייב
moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan reads the mishna as liability where he was forewarned only about it and its offspring
moves.about: the mishna holds him liable even when the second animal was slaughtered for idolatry, in the case where he was forewarned only about it and its offspring

moves.cueHe: ורבי שמעון בן לקיש אמר: כיון דכי אתרו ביה – פטור
moves.summary: Reish Lakish holds him exempt even without forewarning for idolatry
moves.about: whether a transgression carrying death for which no forewarning was given still cancels the lashes incurred for the lighter prohibition

moves.cueHe: ואזדו לטעמייהו
moves.summary: the setama binds each sage's ruling here to his position in a second dispute
moves.about: R' Yoḥanan's ruling here follows the view he holds in Rav Dimi's report about an unwarned severe transgression joined to a monetary penalty

moves.cueHe: דכי אתא רב דימי אמר
moves.summary: Rav Dimi reports the parallel dispute over an unforewarned severe penalty joined to a monetary one
moves.about: Rav Dimi brings R' Yoḥanan's ruling from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia

moves.cueHe: רבי יוחנן אומר: חייב, דהא לא אתרו ביה
moves.summary: the setama supplies each side's reasoning in the reported dispute
moves.about: the rationale of R' Yoḥanan's liability — no forewarning was given for the severe transgression, so only the monetary obligation stands

moves.cueHe: וצריכא, דאי אשמועינן בהא
moves.summary: both statements are needed, since from the idolatry case alone Reish Lakish might have conceded the monetary case
moves.about: why Reish Lakish's exemption had to be stated for the idolatry case and could not be inferred from the monetary case

moves.cueHe: ואי איתמר בהא
moves.summary: and from the monetary case alone R' Yoḥanan might have conceded the idolatry case
moves.about: why R' Yoḥanan's liability had to be stated for the monetary case and could not be inferred from the idolatry case

moves.cueHe: ופרת חטאת שחיטה שאינה ראויה היא? והתניא
moves.summary: a baraita of R' Shimon makes the red heifer's slaughter fit, against the mishna's exemption
moves.about: R' Shimon's own baraita calls the red heifer susceptible to food impurity because it once had a fit moment, so its slaughter should not count as unfit

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש: אומר היה רבי שמעון
moves.summary: Reish Lakish strengthens the objection: R' Shimon holds the heifer redeemable even on its pyre
moves.about: Reish Lakish attributes to R' Shimon the view that the red heifer can still be redeemed even upon its pyre

moves.cueHe: אמר רב שמן בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן: פרת חטאת אינה משנה
moves.summary: the red heifer clause is struck from the mishna
moves.about: the contradiction dissolves because the red heifer clause is not an authentic part of the mishna

moves.cueHe: ועגלה ערופה, לאו שחיטה ראויה היא? והתנן
moves.summary: a mishna lets the heifer graze once the murderer is found, so its slaughter is fit
moves.about: a mishna rules that the heifer whose neck was to be broken goes out to graze if the murderer is found, so before the breaking its slaughter is fit

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש משום רבי ינאי: עגלה ערופה אינה משנה
moves.summary: in R' Yannai's name, the broken-necked heifer clause too is struck from the mishna
moves.about: the objection from the grazing heifer falls away because the broken-necked heifer clause is not an authentic part of the mishna

moves.cueHe: ומי אמר רבי ינאי הכי? והאמר רבי ינאי
moves.summary: R' Yannai elsewhere confesses he forgot when the heifer becomes forbidden
moves.about: R' Yannai elsewhere professes not to know when the heifer becomes forbidden, which is incompatible with his ruling that the clause is spurious

moves.cueHe: ואם איתא, לישני: כאן קודם ירידה, כאן לאחר ירידה
moves.summary: had he held so he could have distinguished before and after the heifer's descent instead
moves.about: had R' Yannai really held the clause spurious he could instead have distinguished slaughter before the heifer's descent from slaughter after it

moves.cueHe: אמר רב פנחס בריה דרב אמי: אנן משמיה דרבי שמעון בן לקיש מתנינן לה
moves.summary: the ruling was taught in Reish Lakish's own name, never as R' Yannai's
moves.about: the contradiction from R' Yannai's dictum falls away because the ruling was never R' Yannai's
